messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates Java code to GNU C++11 code. The code should reads and writes I/O from the console.

samples.content:
<translated_code>
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

class InputReader {
private:
    string line;
    istringstream iss;
public:
    InputReader() {}
    string next() {
        while (getline(cin, line)) {
            if (!line.empty()) {
                iss.clear();
                iss.str(line);
                string token;
                if (iss >> token) return token;
            }
        }
        return "";
    }
    int nextInt() {
        return stoi(next());
    }
};

int longestWords(string line) {
    stringstream ss(line);
    string word;
    int max_len = 0;
    while (getline(ss, word, '_')) {
        max_len = max(max_len, (int)word.length());
    }
    return max_len;
}

string trimParentheses(string input) {
    string temp = input.substr(1, input.length() - 1);
    return temp.substr(0, temp.length() - 1);
}

int main() {
    InputReader in;
    int n = in.nextInt();
    string input = in.next();
    string pattern = "\\([\\w_]*\\)";
    regex r(pattern);
    vector<string> outSite;
    regex_token_iterator<string::iterator> rend;
    regex_token_iterator<string::iterator> it(input.begin(), input.end(), r, -1);
    while (it != rend) {
        outSite.push_back(*it++);
    }
    int longest = 0;
    for (string s : outSite) {
        longest = max(longest, longestWords(s));
    }
    smatch m;
    string temp = input;
    long long numberInside = 0;
    while (regex_search(temp, m, r)) {
        string matched = m[0];
        string inside = trimParentheses(matched);
        stringstream ss(inside);
        string part;
        while (getline(ss, part, '_')) {
            if (!part.empty()) numberInside++;
        }
        temp = m.suffix();
    }
    cout << longest << " " << numberInside << endl;
    return 0;
}
</translated_code>
